sentences.zh: 实际上是为了防御。

sentences.en: You see, so basically, the East Indian Company is principally worried about the threat to India from Afghanistan and from Central Asia.
sentences.zh: 你看，所以基本上，东印度公司主要担心的是来自阿富汗和中亚对印度的威胁。

sentences.en: So they see Iran as a potential ally.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将伊朗视为一个潜在的盟友。

sentences.en: And then by the turn of the sort of 19th century, they understand actually the real threat is coming from Russia.
sentences.zh: 然后到了19世纪左右，他们明白实际上真正的威胁来自俄国。

sentences.en: So Iran then becomes a buffer zone.
sentences.zh: 因此伊朗随后成了一个缓冲区。

sentences.en: In that period, Ali, what's going on in Iran?
sentences.zh: 在那个时期，阿里，伊朗发生了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, who's running it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁在统治它？

sentences.en: What sort of country?
sentences.zh: 是个什么样的国家？

sentences.en: What sort of society is it?
sentences.zh: 是个什么样的社会？

sentences.en: So Iran comes out in the 18th century, a period of quite intense political turmoil.
sentences.zh: 所以伊朗在18世纪走出来，那是一个政治动荡相当激烈的时期。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, you know, it's a bit of a mess in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这，你知道的，在某些方面简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: You get a new dynasty emerges at the end of the 19th century, they emerge into this wider world.
sentences.zh: 你发现19世纪末期一个新的王朝崛起了，他们走入了更广阔的世界。

sentences.en: And they emerge into a world which has quite changed from the one that, you know, Iran left in the sense of the end of the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 他们走进了一个与你们知道的17世纪末期伊朗离开时截然不同的世界。

sentences.en: So you have two imperial powers, basically Britain and India, and the Russian Empire to the north.
sentences.zh: 所以你面临着两大帝国势力，主要是北部的英国与印度，以及俄罗斯帝国。

sentences.en: And they're faced with this new dilemma.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着这个全新的困境。

sentences.en: And what you have in Iran is basically what you, you know, a very traditional pre-modern state facing these two modernizing states, if I can put it that way.
sentences.zh: 你在伊朗看到的情况，基本上就像你所知道的那样，一个非常传统的、前现代的国家正面对着这两个现代化的国家，如果我可以这样表述的话。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, and the challenge is quite severe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，而且这种挑战相当严峻。

sentences.en: And they're very enamored in some ways.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，他们非常着迷。

sentences.en: Enamored maybe is too strong a term, but they're sort of puzzled about what the
sentences.zh: 着迷或许是个用词过猛的词，但他们对于

sentences.en: British and the English are doing in India.
sentences.zh: 英国人和英格兰人在印度做什么感到有些困惑。

sentences.en: You know, why are you there?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你们为什么在那里？

sentences.en: The English and the, you know, what they do is they basically cultivate relations with Iran in order to make it, you know, to bring Iran on side vis-a-vis the Russians.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人以及，你知道的，他们的做法基本上是与伊朗培养关系，以便使它，你知道，使伊朗站在他们一边以对抗俄国人。

sentences.en: And that relationship is quite an interesting relationship as it builds up.
sentences.zh: 随着这种关系的建立，它变得相当有趣。

sentences.en: And the Iranians themselves are fascinated by what the English are doing.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人自己也对英国人的所作所为着迷。

sentences.en: I mean, they sort of see this as an interesting development.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们某种程度上把这视为一个有趣的发展。

sentences.en: It helps, of course, that all these people that go to Iran in this period are very fluent in Persian, understand the idioms, understand the etiquette, know how to navigate it.
sentences.zh: 当然，这段时期所有去伊朗的人都精通波斯语、理解成语、懂得礼仪且知道如何应对，这确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 而且这很管用。

sentences.en: You know, these are individuals, political officers, diplomats, and others who are particularly good at their trade in this period.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些人包括政治官员、外交官以及其他在这段时期非常擅长此道的人。

sentences.en: And the Iranians in that way sort of buy into it.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人也就顺理成章地接受了这一点。

sentences.en: And a number of them, of course, go to England in the early 19th century to learn the secrets of, you know, British success.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中许多人在19世纪初前往英国，去学习，你知道的，英国成功秘诀。

sentences.en: What are the secrets?
sentences.zh: 秘诀是什么？

sentences.en: What do they learn?
sentences.zh: 他们学到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, this is the interesting thing, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这当然是有趣的部分。

sentences.en: What they work out and what the British say to them, when you look at it, the British come at this period, post-Napoleonic wars, was, you know, we're a top nation.
sentences.zh: 他们摸索出的东西以及英国人对他们所说的话——当你审视它时，拿破仑战争之后的英国人来到这里时会说，我们是一个顶尖国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why are we top nation?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们是顶尖国家？

sentences.en: Because we have applied the lessons of the Enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 因为我们应用了启蒙运动的教训。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, it's a thoroughly Enlightenment narrative they come in, and a thoroughly Whiggish narrative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，他们带来的是一个彻头彻尾的启蒙运动叙事，也是一个彻底的辉格党叙事。

sentences.en: And they basically say to the Iranians, they say, and it's very interesting that they say, this is pre-racial dogma and all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上对伊朗人说，而且非常有趣的是他们确实这么说了，这是在种族教条和诸如此类的事情出现之前。

sentences.en: They basically say, you know, 150 years ago, we were a miserable, you know, island race, basically killed our king and did all sorts of nasty things.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上说，你知道的，150年前，我们是一个可怜的，你知道的，岛国种族，基本上杀了自己的国王，还干了各种讨厌的事。

sentences.en: And it was all a bit of a mess.
sentences.zh: 这一切都有点一团糟。

sentences.en: But we applied, you know, three things, you know, discipline, law, education, you know, and look where we are now.
sentences.zh: 但我们应用了，你知道的，三件事，你知道的，纪律、法律、教育，你知道的，看看我们现在在哪里。

sentences.en: And if you do these things too, you can achieve all these things.
sentences.zh: 如果你也做这些事，你就能实现所有这些成就。

sentences.en: And of course, for many Iranians, you know, this is quite an attractive option.
sentences.zh: 当然，对许多伊朗人来说，你知道的，这是一个相当有吸引力的选择。

sentences.en: And so Ali, it's basically, it's part of the great game, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，阿里，这基本上是“大博弈”的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: This great kind of struggle for influence between the Russians and the British.
sentences.zh: 这种俄国与英国之间争夺影响力的巨大斗争。

sentences.en: Do the Iranians, are they more inclined to side with Britain or with Russia?
sentences.zh: 伊朗人，他们更倾向于站在英国一边还是俄国一边？

sentences.en: Which is more appealing to them?
sentences.zh: 哪一个对他们更有吸引力？

sentences.en: They fear Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕俄国。

sentences.en: They fear Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕俄国。

sentences.en: Russia has the propensity to send troops in at a moment's notice.
sentences.zh: 俄国动不动就有派军队驻扎的倾向。

sentences.en: The British don't have that capacity.
sentences.zh: 英国人没有这种能力。

sentences.en: The English don't have that capacity.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人没有这种能力。

sentences.en: They're a naval power.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个海军强国。

sentences.en: They're not keen on sending, you know, troops.
sentences.zh: 他们并不热衷于派遣，你知道的，军队。

sentences.en: It's very expensive.
sentences.zh: 那代价非常昂贵。

sentences.en: At this point, then, Britain is not the kind of satanic figure in the Iranian imagination that it later becomes.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，英国在伊朗人的想象中还不是后来那种恶魔般的形象。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: And this is the core of the issue, of course, is that basically, the problem in the
sentences.zh: 而这当然是问题的核心，基本上，问题在于

sentences.en: relationship between Iran and England, in that sense, is that England represents for the Iranians, particularly reforming Iranians at this time, a sort of an aspirational power.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，伊朗与英国关系中的问题在于，对于伊朗人，尤其是当时要求改革的伊朗人来说，英国代表着一种令人向往的力量。

sentences.en: I mean, they like the political ideals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们喜欢这些政治理想。

sentences.en: What they get annoyed about, I mean, this is a fundamental issue.
sentences.zh: 让他们感到恼火的是——我的意思是，这是一个根本问题。

sentences.en: Iranians have no expectations of Russia whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人对俄国没有任何期望。

sentences.en: Okay, they think it's basically rather brutish in some ways, but, you know, autocracies and all that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们觉得它在某些方面相当粗鲁，但是，你知道的，专制政体以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: So they have no expectations.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有任何期望。

sentences.en: So there's nothing to betray for the English, on the other hand.
sentences.zh: 因此，另一方面，对于英格兰人来说，也就无所谓背叛。

sentences.en: You know, they have this sort of expectation that the British will live up to their ideals, which is rather Whiggish, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们抱有一种期望，即英国人会不负他们的理想，这相当带有辉格党色彩，你知道的。

sentences.en: And then basically, the British don't.
sentences.zh: 然后基本上，英国人却没有做到。

sentences.en: So they go, well, hang on a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会想：等等。

sentences.en: You know, you have all these wonderful ideals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们有所有这些美好的理想。

sentences.en: And why aren't you supporting us in our bids?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们不支持我们的诉求？

sentences.en: You know, this is the thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是这样。

sentences.en: There's that sort of contraSt.
sentences.zh: 存在着那种对比。

sentences.en: And you see this with the Americans too, later in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 你在20世纪后期的美国人身上也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: So Ali, you sent us an excerpt from a thing called the Journal of the Persian Princes.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿里，你给我们发了一段摘录，出自一本叫《波斯王子游记》的书。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So these are guys who've visited England.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人是访问过英国的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when did they visit?
sentences.zh: 他们是什么时候访问的？

sentences.en: So they visited in 1835.
sentences.zh: 他们是在1835年访问的。

sentences.en: And they do a thing.
sentences.zh: 他们做了一件事。

sentences.en: So throughout the early 19th century, you get a series of visitors who come in, look at various aspects of English society, British society.
sentences.zh: 所以在整个19世纪初，你会看到一系列的访客到来，观察英国社会、英国社会的各个方面。

sentences.en: They're enormously impressed by things that we wouldn't instinctively think would be the thing.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们不会本能地认为是重点的东西留下了极其深刻的印象。

sentences.en: But it's things like liberty, freedom.
sentences.zh: 但那是诸如自由之类的东西。

sentences.en: They're fascinated with newspapers.
sentences.zh: 他们对报纸着迷。

sentences.en: They can't understand the concept of newspapers, this idea that you publish 100,000 papers and then bin it and then start again the next day.
sentences.zh: 他们无法理解报纸的概念，这种你发行10万份报纸然后扔掉、第二天又重新开始的想法。

sentences.en: I mean, for them, they sort of go, you know, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对他们来说，他们会觉得，你知道的，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: They're fascinated by, you know, essentially economic development and industry.
sentences.zh: 他们对，你知道的，本质上的经济发展和工业着迷。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they do look at, by the way, interestingly, is the Navy.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们确实观察的一件事，有趣的是，就是海军。

sentences.en: You know, the Navy is something that impresses them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，海军是让他们印象深刻的东西。

sentences.en: The industry behind it, I think, is what impresses them.
sentences.zh: 我想，留下深刻印象的是它背后的工业。

sentences.en: They're never taken around to see, you know, military parades.
sentences.zh: 他们从来没有被带去参观过，你知道的，阅兵式。

sentences.en: That isn't what impresses them.
sentences.zh: 那不是让他们印象深刻的东西。

sentences.en: And they're not.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有。

sentences.en: What they're taken to see is, and the Three Princes do this, is the Thames Tunnel, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们被带去参观的是——三位王子也是这么做的——泰晤士河隧道，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they go, what?
sentences.zh: 所以他们会说：什么？

sentences.en: They're building a tunnel under the river.
sentences.zh: 他们正在河底下建一条隧道。

sentences.en: You know, how the hell is that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Because this is the heyday of Britain as the workshop of the world, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 因为我想这是英国作为世界工厂的全盛时期。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so they recognise that this is the motor of British power, I guess.
sentences.zh: 所以我想他们认识到这是英国力量的发动机。

sentences.en: But they also love the politics, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但他们也很喜欢政治，不是吗？

sentences.en: They've got a brilliant section here about explaining politics to their Persian readers.
sentences.zh: 他们这里有一个精彩的章节，向他们的波斯读者解释政治。

sentences.en: So they say, there's loads of viziers, and all the viziers have vice-viziers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，这里有大量的维齐尔（大臣），所有的维齐尔都有副维齐尔。

sentences.en: Although every one of these viziers is a master of his own department, they do not drink water without the advice of each other.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些维齐尔中的每一个人都是自己部门的主管，但如果没有彼此的建议，他们连水都不喝。

sentences.en: They do nothing without consulting each other.
sentences.zh: 他们做任何事都要互相商量。

sentences.en: Then they go on to explain, they say, basically, the Tories are wigs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们继续解释说，基本上，托利党就是辉格党。

sentences.en: Sometimes the father is a wig and his son a Tory, and two brothers, maybe one a Tory and the other a wig.
sentences.zh: 有时候父亲是辉格党而儿子是托利党，两个兄弟中，可能一个托利党另一个是辉格党。

sentences.en: They say, the difference between the Tories, this is the Tories.
sentences.zh: 他们说，托利党与——这就是托利党。

sentences.en: They say, 300 years ago, we were wild people, and our kingdom then was worse and lower than any other.
sentences.zh: 他们说，300年前，我们是野蛮人，我们当时的王国比任何其他王国都要糟糕和低级。

sentences.en: But through mind, wisdom, and learning, we have brought our kingdom to its present height of honour.
sentences.zh: 但通过思想、智慧和学识，我们将我们的王国带到了目前荣誉的巅峰。

sentences.en: And as our empire grew larger by our management, why should we reform and give up our policy, which has done all this good?
sentences.zh: 随着我们的帝国通过我们的管理而不断壮大，我们为什么要改革并放弃给我们带来如此多好处的政策呢？

sentences.en: So that's Toryism.
sentences.zh: 这就是托利党主义。

sentences.en: And then Wiggism, they say, we know that it is more prudent to go according to the changes of time and circumstances.
sentences.zh: 然后是辉格党主义，他们说，我们知道顺应时代和环境的变化更为明智。

sentences.en: Moreover, by the old policy, only a few were profited.
sentences.zh: 此外，根据旧政策，只有少数人受益。

sentences.en: And as our government is a general one, we must observe that which is best for the whole nation, and that all should be profited, and every person should enjoy the same privileges.
sentences.zh: 由于我们的政府是一个全民政府，我们必须遵循对整个国家最有利的做法，让所有人都受益，每个人都应该享有相同的特权。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not wildly wrong, are they, I suppose?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的看法并不离谱，对吧，我想？

sentences.en: I mean, the interesting thing is, looking at that, and my own sort of like reading through it,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有趣的事情是，看着这些，以及我自己的阅读体验，

sentences.en: is that it's clear that three princes in particular are talking to their interlocutors, in a sense of people like Palmerston.
sentences.zh: 很明显，特别是三位王子在与他们的对话者交流，某种意义上就像帕麦斯顿这样的人。

sentences.en: So it's quite, you know, they're taking a thoroughly red-blooded Wiggism, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 所以这相当，你知道的，我必须说，他们接受了一种非常纯粹的辉格党主义。

sentences.en: They're hanging around with loads of Wigs.
sentences.zh: 他们整天和一大堆辉格党人混在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're basically saying to them, the Tories are all this.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上对他们说，托利党就是这样的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite an interesting quote, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这其实是一段非常有趣的引文。

sentences.en: And, you know, they ingest this thoroughly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们彻底吸收了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, they buy into this narrative, and they want to go back to Iran and say, look, you know, we can do this, we can develop this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们完全接受了这种叙事，并且想回到伊朗说，看，你知道的，我们可以做到这一点，我们可以发展这个。

sentences.en: And of course, the British, for them, you know, this is the way they gain influence.
sentences.zh: 当然，对英国人来说，你知道的，这是他们获得影响力的方式。

sentences.en: So going back to Tom's comment about the great game, the Russians are notorious in Iran for basically using brute force when they want to get their way.
sentences.zh: 因此回到汤姆关于大博弈的评论，俄国人在伊朗是出了名的，当他们想要达到目的时基本上会使用粗暴的武力。

sentences.en: The British, on the other hand, are seen as, you know, much more subtle.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，英国人被视为，你知道的，要微妙得多。

sentences.en: You know, what they're doing is they're, by persuasion, trying to bring people over, you know, you can, you know, see what we've done, emulate us,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在做的是通过说服来把人们争取过来，你知道的，你可以，你知道的，看看我们做过的事，效仿我们，

sentences.en: you know, you know, this is the way to go forward.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你知道的，这才是前进的道路。

sentences.en: And this is the interesting thing, really, about the nature of the relationship, is that I think part of the problems in the
sentences.zh: 这确实是关于这种关系本质的有趣之处，我认为关系中的部分问题在于

sentences.en: relationship is, is the intimacy of it, you know, the ideological intimacy of it, that actually, one of the problems is, is that the Iranians find the British model extremely
sentences.zh: 亲密性，你知道的，意识形态上的亲密性，实际上，问题之一在于伊朗人发现英国模式极其

sentences.en: attractive.
sentences.zh: 有吸引力。

sentences.en: They also know, for instance, that Britain is composed of four different countries, you know, they sort of say it's Wales, Scotland, Ireland, England.
sentences.zh: 他们还知道，例如，英国由四个不同的国家组成，你知道的，他们会说是威尔士、苏格兰、爱尔兰、英格兰。

sentences.en: And they like this idea in their own sort of, they look at their own sort of imperial kingdom, if I can put it that way.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢这种想法，在他们自己的某种程度上，他们审视着他们自己的那种帝国王朝，如果我可以这样表述的话。

sentences.en: And they say, I, this is a way also in which we can manage a sort of a development of a modern, quote, national state.

sentences.en: It's not a, it's something that by the end of the 19th, early 20th century, people are really, really buying into.

sentences.en: And they do this.

sentences.en: But of course, in the 19th century, Freemasonry was very iconoclastic.

sentences.en: It was anti-superstition.

sentences.zh: 它完全是为了创造新的政治现实。

sentences.en: And of course, many, even religious figures in Iran became Freemasons and joined up to this and became
sentences.zh: 当然，伊朗的许多人，甚至宗教人士也成为了共济会员并加入了这一组织，成为了

sentences.en: And it's actually described by some of the leaders as, you know, the spiritual child of Great Britain.

sentences.en: Now, if I was to say that to you, as you say, and your reaction is actually it.

sentences.en: In the context of today, people go, you know, oh, my God, you know, why would anyone say that?

sentences.zh: 但它就在文本里。

sentences.en: aftermath of the revolution is sort of slightly sort of fading, they're losing intereSt. You know, they want, they don't want to annoy the Russians and all this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 之后，已经有点在消退了，他们正在失去兴趣。你知道的，他们想要、他们不想惹恼俄罗斯人以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, the Iranian revolution is saying, well, hang on a minute, this is your baby, and you're dumping on us.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，伊朗革命的意思是，等一下，这是你们的孩子，而你们却在抛弃我们。

sentences.en: It's a critical moment, in my view.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: So, so essentially, the relationship, through the 19th century, there's, there's admiration for Britain on the part of quite a lot of Iranians, particularly the intellectual class.
sentences.zh: 所以，从根本上说，在整个19世纪的关系中，有相当多的伊朗人，尤其是知识分子阶层，对英国充满了钦佩。

sentences.en: Yeah, therefore, also huge scope for disappointment.
sentences.zh: 是的，因此，这也带来了巨大的失望空间。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 其核心思想其实是，因为你有着巨大的

sentences.zh: 钦佩，所以当英国人没有兑现承诺时，你就会感到失望。

sentences.zh: 他说，你们为废除奴隶贸易做了那么多，却什么也不做来帮我们，你知道的，应付中亚的奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: And why don't you help us?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么不帮我们？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, there are obvious reasons why the British don't do anything, you know, but it's interesting enough, the British
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，英国人不采取任何行动有显而易见的原因，你知道的，但很有趣的是，英国

sentences.en: official says, you know, he says, you know, to be honest, the prince had a point, you know, I mean,
sentences.zh: 官员说，你知道的，他说，老实说，王子确实有道理，你知道的，我的意思是，

sentences.en: you know, we're not actually, you know, we're not helping them really, in some of this stuff with these raids from Turkmen raiders and whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，实际上我们并没有，你知道的，我们在对付土库曼人的突袭和其他事情上，并没有真正帮到他们什么。

sentences.en: But he says, you know, I don't understand how can you be so you know, you're well known internationally, this is in the 1850s, I think 1860.
sentences.zh: 但他说，你知道的，我不明白你怎么能这样，你知道的，你在国际上很有名，这是在1850年代，我想是1860年。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't want to say let's not get too carried away and say it's all rosy, because of course, there was a there was a very brief Anglo Persian war in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不想说，我们别太得意忘形，说一切都很顺利，因为当然，在19世纪50年代发生了一场非常短暂的英波战争。

sentences.en: The interesting thing about the Anglo Persian war, which was about Afghanistan, was that the
sentences.zh: 关于英波战争，这场战争是因阿富汗而起的，有趣的是

sentences.en: British, actually, at the end of the war, had a very lenient treaty on it.
sentences.zh: 英国人实际上在战争结束时，对它实行了非常宽大的条约。

sentences.en: I mean, they didn't, it was not a punitive treaty.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们没有，这不是一项惩罚性的条约。

sentences.en: And of course, ironically, or paradoxically, what happens after
sentences.zh: 当然，具有讽刺意味或矛盾的是，在

sentences.zh: 1857年之后发生的事情是，它为英国思想打开了更大的一扇门，因为知识分子说，实际上，你知道，这场战争，你知道，让我们把它抛在脑后吧。

sentences.zh: 在某些方面与英国人合作也许确实有其可取之处。

sentences.en: And of course, the British then get involved in a series of economic concessions, partly in a bid by some people,
sentences.zh: 当然，英国随后又参与了一系列经济特许权，部分是一些人的企图，

sentences.en: they sort of say, let's get economic investment in because that will catalyze reform.
sentences.zh: 他们有点像在说，让我们引进经济投资，因为这会催化改革。

sentences.zh: 但当然，这引出了我们，我想是英伊关系的下一个重大方面，即在伊朗建立石油工业。

sentences.en: And that's obviously a critical factor as well.
sentences.zh: 这显然也是一个关键因素。

sentences.zh: 所以我们休息一下。

sentences.zh: 我们今天将与阿里·安萨里（Ali Ansari）一起探讨英伊关系。

sentences.en: And Ali, you have taken us up to the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 阿里，你已经把我们带到了20世纪。

sentences.en: Things between Britain and Iran.
sentences.zh: 英国和伊朗之间的关系。

sentences.en: There are aspects of Britain that people in Iran admire.
sentences.zh: 英国的某些方面是受到伊朗人赞赏的。

sentences.en: But with the 20th century, things start to go downhill, do they?
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪，情况开始走下坡路了，是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, the interesting thing is, is that there are a number of episodes in the 19th century, which don't go particularly well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，你知道，有趣的是，19世纪发生了许多事件，进展得并不是特别顺利。

sentences.en: There's obviously the, you know, the war, which we mentioned, there's a tobacco revolt in 1891.
sentences.zh: 显然有我们提到的战争，1891年的烟草暴动。

sentences.en: But interestingly enough, you know, even in 1906, as I said, you know, when you get this constitutional revolution, they still talk about it as the
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你知道，即使在1906年，正如我所说，当你经历这场立宪革命时，他们仍然称其为

sentences.zh: 大英帝国的精神之子。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并非无足轻重。

sentences.zh: 它，

sentences.en: Nobody bothers about that yet.
sentences.zh: 还没有人对此感到困扰。

sentences.en: let's give, you know, the little Satan a good kicking and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 让我们好好教训一下小撒旦，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I think for the vast majority of people, actually, it's not going to be ideological at all.
sentences.zh: 我认为对绝大多数人来说，实际上，这根本不是意识形态问题。

sentences.en: I think they'll quite like the fact that they're playing England.
sentences.zh: 我想他们会挺高兴能和英格兰踢球的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's a lot of, to be honest, interest and fascination with the Premier League,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说实话，大家对英超联赛、

sentences.en: English football, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 英格兰足球等等有着极大的兴趣和迷恋。

sentences.en: I mean, they love it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们太喜欢了。

sentences.en: So I think in some ways, they'll find it quite interesting and, you know, there'll be less vitriol.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，我想他们会觉得这很有趣，而且，你知道的，敌意会少一些。

sentences.en: I mean, just to give you an example of how the mood has changed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，举个例子来说明气氛是如何改变的。

sentences.en: A few years ago, there was an election in Iran.
sentences.zh: 几年前，伊朗举行了一场选举。

sentences.en: And for some reason, you know, the hardliner said, you know, we must vote for the people that, you know, Britain has said we mustn't vote, you know, because basically there's some
sentences.zh: 由于某种原因，你知道的，强硬派说，你知道的，我们绝不能投票给那些，你知道的，英国人说我们不能投票的人，因为基本上有某个

sentences.en: British, I think the Persian service had said something like, you know, vote for these people.
sentences.zh: 英国机构，我想是波斯语广播部曾说过类似的话，比如，投票给这些人。

sentences.en: And they said, these are British stooges, don't vote for them.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这些是英国的走狗，不要投他们。

sentences.en: And in actual fact, when the vote came in, they all voted for exactly those people.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，当投票结果出来时，他们全都投给了正是这些人。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, they ignored their own government and said, actually, you know, we think these people are decent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，他们无视了自己的政府，并表示，实际上，你知道的，我们觉得这些人很正派。

sentences.en: So again, it's, I think there's a much, much more nuanced appreciation of Britain among the
sentences.zh: 所以再次说明，我认为公众对英国有着一种更加、更加细致入微的看法，

sentences.en: general public, certainly now, where there's much less adherence to what the official narrative is coming out of the government.
sentences.zh: 当然是在现在，大家对政府官方说辞的盲从已经少得多了。

sentences.en: And the Iranian footballers themselves have quite prominently, some of them have quite prominently supported the campaign against the headscarf.
sentences.zh: 而且伊朗足球运动员自己也非常引人注目，其中一些人非常显眼地支持了反头巾运动。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, in previous occasions, these sort of quote, celebrities, sporting celebrities haven't really said anything, they've kept studiously neutral.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在过去，这些所谓的名人、体育明星并没有真正表态，他们一直刻意保持中立。

sentences.en: Now they're coming out, there's a couple of leading, I mean, they're managers now, they're player managers and managers.
sentences.zh: 现在他们站出来了，有几个领军人物，我是说，他们现在是教练了，身兼球员兼教练和纯教练。

sentences.en: But, you know, heroes of the previous World Cup and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，上届世界杯的英雄之类的。

sentences.en: I mean, they've basically come out very much in support of the protesters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们基本上非常公开地站出来支持抗议者。

sentences.en: And the governments actually find it quite difficult to know what to do about them.
sentences.zh: 而政府实际上觉得很难知道该拿他们怎么办。

sentences.en: Because they are immensely popular figures in Iran itself.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在伊朗本土是极具人气的人物。

sentences.en: And it's difficult to underestimate how popular football is, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，很难低估足球有多受欢迎。

sentences.en: I mean, that's another example of the influence of Britain, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是英国影响力的另一个例证，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the popularity of football in Iran is enormous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，足球在伊朗的普及度是巨大的。

sentences.en: It is, in effect, the national sport.
sentences.zh: 它实际上就是国民运动。

sentences.en: I mean, most people talk about wrestling as the national sport.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大多数人把摔跤称为国民运动。

sentences.en: Just on that question about enduring British influence, something that always fascinates me is whether people learn British or American English.
sentences.zh: 顺着关于英国持久影响力的问题，一直让我着迷的是，人们学的是英式英语还是美式英语。

sentences.en: So in Iran, would they learn, would they still have that sort of 19th century sense of Britain as prestigious and whatnot?
sentences.zh: 所以在伊朗，他们会学吗？他们仍然保留那种19世纪视英国为享有声望之国的观念吗？

sentences.en: And would they adopt
sentences.zh: 他们会采用

sentences.en: British accents when they speak English?
sentences.zh: 说英语时的英国口音吗？

sentences.en: Or would they do what a lot of people now do and learn
sentences.zh: 还是会像现在许多人那样去学

sentences.en: American English?
sentences.zh: 美式英语？

sentences.en: I think it's, I mean, from my own experience, and limited as it is at the moment, I mean, I think it's,
sentences.zh: 我认为，从我自己的经验来看——尽管目前还很有限——我是说，我认为，

sentences.en: you know, their English is learned from films, songs, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们的英语是从电影、歌曲等途径学来的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of learned secondhand.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这算是一种二手习得。

sentences.en: And by and large, it would be, I don't know if you call it American or British English, it's almost like an international English, if I could put it that way.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我不知道你该叫它美式英语还是英式英语，如果我可以这样表达的话，它几乎就像是一种国际英语。

sentences.en: But it's certainly, you know, I think the important point here is that English is the sort of second language in Iran.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道的，我认为这里的重点是英语是伊朗的某种第二语言。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这才是最有趣的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, people will learn English, they see English as the language that they need to learn to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们会学英语，他们把英语视为为了出人头地而必须学习的语言。

sentences.en: And they're pretty good at it, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 而且我得说，他们学得相当不错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very interesting how cosmopolitan, you know, the Iranians have been.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，伊朗人表现得如此具有世界主义色彩，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And if you go back even, you know, the past 200 years, there's a there's a wonderful anecdote to the first Persian ambassador who came to Britain in 1809.
sentences.zh: 如果你甚至回溯到过去200年，关于1809年首位来到英国的波斯大使，有一个非常精彩的轶事。

sentences.en: And he starts to learn English, you know, as soon as he arrives.
sentences.zh: 他一抵达就开始学英语，你知道的。

sentences.en: And apparently, the Ottoman ambassador comes into and says, what on earth are you doing?
sentences.zh: 显然，奥斯曼帝国的大使走进来问：你到底在干什么？

sentences.en: And he says, well, I'm learning English.
sentences.zh: 他说：嗯，我在学英语。

sentences.en: He says, what, what for?
sentences.zh: 对方说：什、什么为了？

sentences.en: He said, well, I'm ambassador to Britain, you know, he says, I've been here two years, and I can't speak a word.
sentences.zh: 他说：嗯，我是驻英国大使，你知道的，他说：我已经来了两年了，却连一个字都不会说。

sentences.en: And he sort of said, well, I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对方就说：嗯，我是说，好吧。

sentences.en: And the Persian ambassador, that's very odd.
sentences.zh: 波斯大使说：这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I mean, so it's very interesting how they've sort of they're able to absorb, I mean, there's a certain,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，所以这非常有趣，他们是如何能够吸收的，我是说，有一种，

sentences.en: you know, going back to Herodotus, and the ability of the Persians to sort of adopt and adapt, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，追溯到希罗多德，波斯人那种采纳和适应的能力，诸如此类。

sentences.en: There's a certain truth to that.
sentences.zh: 这确实有一定的道理。

sentences.en: They're very engaged.
sentences.zh: 他们非常投入。

sentences.en: And I'm always very impressed today with the Iranians as isolated as they are in many ways from the outside world and communications, not as much as people reckon.
sentences.zh: 今天，伊朗人与外界在许多方面如此隔绝，通讯也没有人们想象的那么多，但我总是对他们印象深刻。

sentences.en: But still, even, you know, their fluency in English is impressive, given they don't really get access.
sentences.zh: 不过即便如此，鉴于他们并没有真正的接触渠道，他们流利的英语依然令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: So Ali, one last thing before we go, this thing about the old fox I read about.
sentences.zh: 那么阿里，在我们离开前的最后一件事，我读到关于那个老狐狸的事。

sentences.en: So there's a poet, isn't there, called Pishavari?
sentences.zh: 所以有一位诗人生于，是叫皮沙瓦里吗？

sentences.en: And his father was killed in that war that you mentioned in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲在您提到的1850年代的那场战争中丧生。

sentences.en: And he wrote this poem.
sentences.zh: 他写了这首诗。

sentences.en: The translation is, many an ancient house was raised after you crept in.
sentences.zh: 翻译过来是：在你潜入之后，不知多少古老的宅邸拔地而起。

sentences.en: You seize lands through your fox games.
sentences.zh: 你通过你狡猾的把戏掠夺土地。

sentences.en: You have escaped hundreds of traps like an old fox.
sentences.zh: 你像老狐狸一样逃过了数百个陷阱。

sentences.en: And that's us.
sentences.zh: 而那就是我们。

sentences.en: That's the British.
sentences.zh: 那是英国人。

sentences.en: And is that an expression that Iranians still use?
sentences.zh: 这仍然是伊朗人使用的表达吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they had a huge poster in 2016 of a fox in a huge jack waistcoat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在2016年，他们曾制作过一张巨大的海报，上面画着一只穿着巨大斜纹呢背心的狐狸。

sentences.en: That could be a kind of World Cup icon.
sentences.zh: 那可以算是一种世界杯标志了。

sentences.en: It could be.
sentences.zh: 确实可以。

sentences.en: That should be our mascots.
sentences.zh: 那应该成为我们的吉祥物。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it basically says, you know, the evil state of Britain has always been an eternal enemy of Iran.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是在说，你知道的，英国这个邪恶国家一直是伊朗不共戴天的敌人。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, historically, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，从历史角度来看，这不是真的。

sentences.en: But there you are, you know, that's what they'll put out.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，你知道的，他们就是会宣扬这些。

sentences.en: And again, the irony of it is, is that if you look at regional histories, you know, they always look at the Persians as extremely cunning, you know, the Persians,
sentences.zh: 再次说明，讽刺的是，如果你看看地区历史，你知道，他们总是把波斯人视为极其狡猾，你知道的，波斯人，

sentences.en: the ones that you sedition to get what they want.
sentences.zh: 那些煽动叛乱以达到目的的人。

sentences.en: And ironically, what the Iranians are now doing is transferring that onto the British, because actually, the British have done it better as far as So we're both cunning.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，伊朗人现在所做的是把这一点转移到英国人身上，因为实际上，就……所以我们都很狡猾。

sentences.en: I mean, we can both be cunning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都可以很狡猾。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we're both foxes.
sentences.zh: 而且我们都是狐狸。

sentences.en: You know, it's also, but I think, you know, the justification for it, if I can put it that way,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这也是，但我认为，如果我这样表达的话，其背后的理由

sentences.en: is this actually fundamental point that while politics was, the British politics was always attractive to Iranians, they always felt deeply disappointed by British policy.
sentences.zh: 正是这个根本点：虽然政治，英国政治对伊朗人总是有吸引力的，但他们总是对英国政策感到深深的失望。

sentences.en: And they always didn't understand why, you know, the British didn't live up to the standards that they held themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们总是不明白为什么，你知道的，英国人没有达到他们自己所标榜的标准。

sentences.en: And the sad thing is, I think, from my perspective, is that there's a host of
sentences.zh: 而可悲的是，从我的角度来看，有成群的

sentences.en: British diplomats who will accept this.
sentences.zh: 英国外交官会接受这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at their private communications, they say, you know, what we're doing here is we're letting people down.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看看他们的私人信件，他们会说，你知道的，我们在这里做的事是在让人们失望。

sentences.en: You know, these are our friends, and we're letting them down.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些是我们的朋友，而我们在让他们失望。

sentences.en: And for that, that's a great tragedy, actually.
sentences.zh: 而对于这一点，实际上是一个巨大的悲剧。

sentences.en: And I mean, one hopes that going forward, things can be changed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们希望在未来，事情能够有所改变。

sentences.en: Well, that's a fine note on which to end.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个很好的收尾。

sentences.en: Ali, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 阿里，非常感谢。

sentences.en: And may the best team win.
sentences.zh: 祝最好的球队获胜。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Thanks all for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余烬》（The Rest is History）。
